title: Cloud Migration Strategy
subtitle: A phased plan for moving core workloads to the cloud

slides.title: Cloud Migration Strategy
slides.subtitle: A phased plan for moving core workloads to the cloud
slides.speaker_notes: This deck proposes a phased approach to migrating our core applications. All cost figures are illustrative planning estimates.

slides.title: Our on-premise estate is limiting speed and resilience
bullets: Hardware refresh for 60% of servers is due within 18 months
New environments take weeks to provision instead of minutes
Disaster recovery is tested once a year and only partially
Peak demand forces us to pay for idle capacity year-round
slides.speaker_notes: The refresh cycle gives us a natural decision point: reinvest in hardware, or move workloads to the cloud.

slides.title: Most workloads can be rehosted or replatformed

chart.title: Application portfolio by migration path
chart.source_note: Illustrative data - based on a sample portfolio assessment

slides.speaker_notes: Only around one in eight applications needs significant re-engineering. The majority can move with limited code change, which keeps risk and cost down.

slides.title: Phased migration balances speed and risk
slides.speaker_notes: Phase 1 builds the guardrails and earns confidence on lower-risk systems. Phase 2 moves the critical workloads once the foundations are proven.

slides.title: Run costs fall below on-premise from year two
bullets: Year one carries dual-running and migration costs
Savings come from rightsizing and retiring idle capacity
Payback expected within about three years

chart.title: Annual infrastructure cost (planning estimate)
chart.source_note: Illustrative data - planning estimate, not a quote

slides.speaker_notes: The first year costs more because we run both environments. From year two the cloud option is cheaper, and the gap widens as we optimise.

slides.title: Decisions needed today
bullets: Approve Phase 1 budget and landing-zone design
Confirm the cloud provider shortlist for final evaluation
Nominate business owners for the first ten applications
Agree a target date to exit the primary data centre
slides.speaker_notes: We are asking for four decisions so Phase 1 can start next month.
